headline: The Biggest Mistakes to Avoid With Your ADU Build
articleBody:
Building an ADU is an exciting investment, but a few common missteps can quickly lead to budget overruns and frustrating delays. Knowing what to watch out for from the very beginning can make all the difference.

One of the most frequent mistakes is underestimating the 'soft costs.' Homeowners create a budget for construction but forget about everything else. Line items for architectural design, structural engineering, site surveys, and city permit fees can add up. It's crucial that your total budget accounts for these expenses, as well as potential utility hookup fees, from day one.

Another issue we often see is neglecting utility capacity. You have to confirm that your property's existing electrical service, water line, and sewer connection can support the new dwelling. Discovering a needed upgrade late in the game can cause significant delays and unexpected costs right when you're trying to pass final inspections. A good contractor assesses this early on.

Finally, don't start any work before you have approved permits in hand. It's tempting to get a head start on demolition or site prep, but doing so can create massive problems. Working without permits can lead to fines, stop-work orders, and having to tear down what you've already built. The best way to avoid these pitfalls is with careful, professional planning.
